extracted.intended_audience: students, translators, and scholars of Old English literature (editors of Beowulf)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing an annotated English translation/edition of Beowulf that renders the Old English poetry while documenting textual variants, emendations, and interpretive uncertainties. The work combines poetic translation with critical footnotes and editorial apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and justify emendations and alternate readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the manuscript is unclear or critics propose variants, state the emendation and its effect on the text (e.g. "If S.'s emendation be accepted, v.57 will read: ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the suggested emendation, show the resulting reading, cite the critic(s) proposing it (S., Grdtvg., M., etc.), and explain why the emendation clarifies or improves the sense. Examples on the page show multiple suggested readings and their syntactic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and account for alliteration and metrical features
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing words or word-order, consider how the choice affects Old English poetic devices (e.g. "'on' bears the alliteration; cf. 'on hafu' (2524)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer readings that maintain or reasonably reflect the original alliterative pattern; when a choice sacrifices alliteration for sense, note that trade-off in the commentary and, where possible, present alternatives that preserve meter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide literal and sense-rendering options with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a primary translation and record alternative glosses or renderings for difficult words or constructions (e.g. multiple renderings of 'meodu-scencum', 'fenne').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which reading is used in the main text, give literal glosses in notes, and explain the translator's preference (clarity, fidelity, poetic effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate textual cruxes and ambiguous passages explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag lines or phrases that are 'least understood' or 'open to dispute' and summarize the nature of the difficulty (lexical, syntactic, emendatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the competing interpretations, list why words are problematic, and, where appropriate, propose the most defensible interpretation while leaving uncertainty visible (e.g. discussion of v.1599 / the problematic sentence noted as 'least understood').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and cite critical authorities and variant editions
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussing readings or translations, reference editors/critics (abbreviated names appear throughout: B., K., Gr., H.-So., t.B., etc.) and indicate which readings derive from which editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent abbreviations, name the edition or scholar responsible for a suggested reading, and explain how their proposals affect translation and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply concise sectional summaries or headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide short bracketed summaries for narrative blocks (e.g. '{Beowulf's farewell.}' '{The Geats prepare to leave Dane-land.}').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brief, neutral headings to orient readers to scene breaks, speakers, and major narrative shifts; these assist comprehension without altering the poetic text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gloss cultural terms, names, kennings, and compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Render or gloss culturally specific expressions, names, and kennings (e.g. 'Sea-Geats', 'victory-Scyldings', compound words like 'eaforhéafodsegn').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either translate such terms or provide a succinct explanatory note; where a compound is uncertain, discuss alternative segmentations and their implications for meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain syntactic rearrangements and translator insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the translator alters word-order or supplies words for sense (substitutions like 'and gives no gold-plated rings, in order to incite the recipient to boastfulness'), note such interventions and the textual motive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between literal readings and translator-added clarifications; justify insertions as necessary for modern comprehension or to restore sense where the text is corrupt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve proper names and genealogical identifications; identify roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep Old English names and label their tribal/kinship roles (e.g. 'Ecgtheow's offspring', 'kinsman of Healfdene', 'Hrethel's son Higelac'), clarifying relationships in notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not obscure lineage and social roles; annotate relationships that bear on the narrative or on succession/kingdom matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about variant translations of key lexemes and their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: For recurrent or pivotal words (e.g. 'geworhte'/'geþóhte', 'wunað'/'wunade'), present the variant readings, translate each variant, and state how each reading alters the verse meaning or tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show sample renderings, as the notes do, and, when one reading is chosen, explain why it was preferred (syntactic clarity, poetic appropriateness, manuscript support).
